details: Bitcoin has officially confirmed a "golden cross," a bullish technical indicator where its 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) crossed above its 200-day EMA around September 11. This is the first such bullish crossover since November 2025's death cross. This development is sparking optimism among investors, even as odds for a Federal Reserve rate hike next week have surged to approximately 85.6% following August's hot core Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. Despite a fourth consecutive day of spot Bitcoin ETF outflows totaling around $462.6 million for the week (September 8-11), Bitcoin initially held its gains, trading near $77,269.
title: Bitcoin Golden Cross Sparks Optimism Amidst Fed Hike Concerns

details: The CLARITY Act, aiming to establish definitive regulations for digital assets in the US, is heading for a significant milestone in the Senate. Lawmakers are scheduled to debate the bill next week, with a major procedural vote anticipated on Tuesday, September 15. Amid ongoing negotiations, President Donald Trump met with advisors on Friday to discuss proposed ethics rules for the crypto bill, fueling concerns about the ability of officials to profit from cryptocurrency investments. Senator Cynthia Lummis has reportedly warned Democrats ahead of the vote, while banks are split over stablecoin yield provisions.
title: CLARITY Act Nears Senate Debate with Ethics Discussions

details: According to on-chain analytics firm CryptoQuant, Bitcoin's outlook remains bullish, but it faces significant resistance at $81,700, which it must clear to confirm the start of a new bull market. Additional resistance levels are identified at $83,600 and $88,700. Bitcoin's recent 24% rally over two weeks has stalled, with the price currently hovering around $77,000, after moving between $76,000 and $82,000. CryptoQuant identifies potential support levels at $70,000 and between $62,000 and $65,000, where long-term holders accumulated approximately 476,000 BTC this year.
title: CryptoQuant: Bitcoin Must Clear $81,700 for New Bull Market Confirmation

details: Germany's finance ministry has drafted a bill on September 9 to end its one-year tax-free rule for cryptocurrencies bought after 2026. The proposed legislation would impose a flat 25% tax on gains from newly acquired crypto, along with a 5.5% surcharge. Cryptocurrencies purchased before this cutoff date will still be subject to the old rule, allowing for tax-free sales after a 12-month holding period. The ministry estimates this change could generate 160 million euros by 2028 and 350 million by 2031. This move signals the end of a tax-free era for new crypto investments in Germany, a development that could dampen long-term holding appetite.
title: Germany to End Tax-Free Rule for New Crypto Holdings

details: Two cryptocurrency billionaires have collectively donated 72 million pounds ($97 million) to the anti-immigration Reform UK party, led by Nigel Farage, over the weekend. Ben Delo, co-founder of BitMEX, gave £36 million ($48 million), which was then matched by crypto investor Christopher Harborne. This record-breaking political donation in British history has ignited concerns about the influence of large sums of money in UK politics. The Reform party has stated that if it gains power, it would advocate for legislation to expand cryptocurrency adoption in Britain, including reductions to capital gains tax on digital assets and the creation of a Bitcoin reserve fund at the Bank of England.
title: Crypto Billionaires Donate $97M to UK's Reform Party, Raising Concerns

details: Revolut has announced that customer Know Your Customer (KYC) data and Bitcoin transaction data were exposed following a fake request from a government domain. This security incident raises concerns about data privacy and the vulnerability of customer information held by cryptocurrency-related platforms.
title: Revolut Reports Exposure of Customer KYC and Bitcoin Data
